prerequisites: Knowledge of dynamics of machine systems
Passing the exam of Meccanica Applicata alle Macchine

learning_outcomes.text: Provide theoretical fundamentals about integration between mechanical, electronic and hydraulic subsystems together with traditional control methodologies.
Utilize software tools for simulation purposes.
Perform experiments on teaching setups designed for tailored mechanical systems with feedback control.
Understand operations, scopes and performances expected from typical devices in automatic plants in the industrial area and within industrial engineering environment.
Assess the dynamic response of systems and devices using wide application methodology.
Apply methodologies learnt in classes to case studies and problems through simulation exercises.
Stimulate autonomous judgement skill for comparing engineering solutions in the framework of automation and control, through solid and shared criteria.
Illustrate and discuss solutions to simulation problems, discuss proposed technical solutions, and learn comparison strategies and trade-offs with alternatives.
Be able to apply and update acquired knowledge in contexts different from those presented during the course, considering technological progress and innovation.

syllabus_topics: Sensors and actuators for mechanical systems control
Sensors to acquire displacement and speed
Examples and models of electric actuators
Harmonic drive and gear reducers for robotics
Role of transmission ratio in steady-states and transients
Teaching lab setups: Twin Rotors and Anti-lock Braking System
assessment_rules: The assessment is through a computer simulation test and an oral test, the latter replaceable by a group project. The simulation exercise is graded on originality, correct mathematical model, algorithm complexity, and control solution versatility. The group project is graded on topic depth, completeness of analysis, operating principles, and context in modern industry. The final grade (out of thirty, with 'Lode' for excellence) depends on overall maturity. A minimum grade of 18/30 requires correct system modeling, clear problem understanding, and sufficient course knowledge. Higher grades are for accurate simulation results with limited uncertainties, and 30/30 for sound qualitative and quantitative solutions with deep knowledge. 'Lode' is for students who formulate solutions in broader engineering contexts, even with unusual problems.
